definitions.explanation: A fermented mixture of rice bran, salt, and water used as a pickling medium for vegetables. The paste is maintained and reused over months or years, developing complex flavors.

examples.japanese: ぬかみそ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{毎日|まいにち}→毎日：00729_mainichi⟧⟦かき{混|ま}ぜる→かき混ぜる：15739_kakimazeru⟧。
examples.english: I stir the rice-bran paste every day.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖母|そぼ}→祖母：00813_sobo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ぬかみそ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{何十年|なんじゅうねん}→何十年：30624_nanjuunen⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{使|つか}い→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦{続|つづ}け→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧て⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: My grandmother's rice-bran paste has been in use for decades.
If you don't add salt to the rice-bran paste, the flavor becomes too weak.

notes:
Also written as {糠味噌|ぬかみそ}. Composed of ⟦{糠|ぬか}→糠：29202_nuka⟧ (rice bran) + ⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧ (miso, fermented paste), though ぬかみそ is not actually miso — the name comes from its paste-like texture. Maintaining a ぬかみそ{床|どこ} (pickling bed) is a traditional household skill passed down through generations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぬかみそ{漬|づ}け: vegetables pickled in rice-bran paste
- ぬかみそ{床|どこ}: the rice-bran pickling bed
- ぬかみそ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かき{混|ま}ぜる→かき混ぜる：15739_kakimazeru⟧: to stir the rice-bran paste
- ぬかみそ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{臭|くさ}い→臭い：01133_kusai⟧: the rice-bran paste smells

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {糠床|ぬかどこ}: rice-bran pickling bed — the container of ぬかみそ used for pickling
- ⟦{漬物|つけもの}→漬物：04938_tsukemono⟧: pickles — the general term for all Japanese pickled vegetables
- ⟦{味噌|みそ}→味噌：01037_miso⟧: miso — fermented soybean paste (different product despite the shared name element)
